subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close or replace the open conflicting fork PR before allowing a fresh narrow fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and narrow, but ClawSweeper should not queue a new fix while an open linked PR with closing syntax still exists unless maintainers decide that fork PR is no longer the landing candidate.

options.title: Close or supersede the fork candidate
options.body: Treat the open fork PR as obsolete because it conflicts, cannot be maintainer-edited, and targets the removed handler, then allow a fresh narrow fix against `approval-handler.runtime.ts`.

options.title: Ask for a fork rewrite
options.body: Have the fork PR author replace the branch with the active-runtime fix shape and provide real Telegram proof before reconsidering it.

options.title: Keep waiting on manual review
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on maintainer triage of the linked fork PR, accepting that the current bug remains unresolved on main.

recommendation.title: Close or supersede the fork candidate
recommendation.body: Treat the open fork PR as obsolete because it conflicts, cannot be maintainer-edited, and targets the removed handler, then allow a fresh narrow fix against `approval-handler.runtime.ts`.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current native approval lifecycle and are the clearest owner-history signal for deciding whether to replace the obsolete handler-path PR.
